title: The supported-Hom identification is the closed-support adjunction transpose
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-pc-scheme] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on the small pro-etale site with constant coefficient sheaf $A_X$ and derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with $i_*$ the underived module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] and shifts $(K[a])^r=K^{r+a}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_i:D(A)\rightleftarrows D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):R\Gamma_Z$ be the derived adjunction specified in [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product], with $C_i(A)=i_*A_Z$ in degree zero; it is normalized there by requiring that the underived adjoint of $a:M\to\Gamma_Z(F)$, precomposed with the quotient $q_i:\underline M_X\to C_i(M)$, is the constant-sheaf adjoint of $a$ followed by $\Gamma_Z(F)\subseteq\Gamma(X,F)$. Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of $A_X$-module sheaves and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Identify $H^a_Z(X,F)=H^aR\Gamma_Z(X,F)$ [def-pur-support-cohomology] with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A[-a],R\Gamma_Z(X,F))$ by sending a class to the map carrying $1$ in degree $a$ to a representing cocycle. For $x\in H^a_Z(X,F)$ let $x^\flat:C_i(A)[-a]=C_i(A[-a])\to F$ be its adjoint under $C_i\dashv R\Gamma_Z$. Then the natural isomorphism $\chi^a_{i,F}:H^a_Z(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)}(i_*A_Z,F[a])$ of [lem-pur-supported-hom], with the following explicit normalization, satisfies
$$\chi^a_{i,F}(x)=x^\flat[a].$$
Here $\chi^a_{i,F}$ is the canonical supported-Hom isomorphism obtained by deriving the inverse of the underived evaluation bijection $v_M:\operatorname{Hom}(i_*A_Z,M)\to\Gamma_Z(X,M)$, $v_M(\varphi)=\varphi_X(q_i(1))$, and then applying the injective-resolution identification of cohomology of derived Hom with derived-category morphisms [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof]. Equivalently, both identifications are derived from the same underived bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*A_Z,M)\cong\Gamma_Z(X,M)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_X(q_i(1))$. No finiteness hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Step 5, "=\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g) by naturality and associativity of supported cup products": the supported cup product and the exterior product of classes with supports must read classes through the same supported-Hom identification (agent-formulated normalization).

proof.text: Put $P=C_i(A)=i_*A_Z$ and $G=\Gamma_Z(X,-)$. For a sheaf $M$, write $b:A\to G(M)$ for the underived adjoint of $\varphi:P\to M$. The normalization in [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] says that $\varphi q_i$ is the constant-sheaf adjoint of $A\xrightarrow{b}G(M)\hookrightarrow\Gamma(X,M)$. Evaluation at $1$ therefore gives $\varphi_X(q_i(1))=b(1)$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A,G(M))$ with $G(M)$, with inverse $s\mapsto(a\mapsto as)$. Consequently the adjunction gives exactly the bijection $v_M$ displayed in the statement. Its inverse sends $s$ to the adjoint $f_s:P\to M$ of $a\mapsto as$. Both maps are additive and $A$-linear; for example the precomposites with the quotient $q_i$ of $f_{s+t}$ and $f_s+f_t$ agree, hence so do these maps. Naturality gives $v_N(k\varphi)=G(k)v_M(\varphi)$ for every $k:M\to N$.

source.place: Underived normalized adjunction; evaluation of the normalization at 1

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal B=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ on the chosen small skeleton [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The coefficient ring sheaf is commutative, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] makes $\mathcal B$ Grothendieck and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies enough injectives. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] to the given bounded-below $F$ on this small ringed site. Fix a quasi-isomorphism $e:F\to I$ with $I$ bounded below, termwise injective and K-injective. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies $RG(QI)$ with $Q(GI)$ via the derived unit $\beta_I:Q(GI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(QI)$. Thus a supported class $x$ is represented by a cocycle $s\in G(I^a)$, transported along $\beta_I$ and $RG(Qe)^{-1}$, as prescribed by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Here $Q$ denotes localization in the appropriate complex category.

Apply step 1 in each degree of $I$. Naturality with respect to $d_I^r$ gives $v_{I^{r+1}}(d_I^r\varphi)=G(d_I^r)v_{I^r}(\varphi)$, so $v_I:\operatorname{Hom}(P,I)\to G(I)$ is an isomorphism of cochain complexes. It sends the cocycle $f_s:P\to I^a$ to $s$. This termwise natural isomorphism derives to the canonical isomorphism between the two right derived functors: by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], derive $v$ and $v^{-1}$, and their composites are identities by the uniqueness there, since their precomposites with the derived units are identities. Clause (2) identifies this comparison on $I$ with precisely $Qv_I$. The same computation applies to the underlying additive Hom complex: its cocycles and boundaries are the underlying groups of the displayed $A$-module complex. Hence the derived inverse used to normalize $\chi$ carries $x$ to the class represented by $f_s$.

source.place: Tags 05TH, 05TI; uniqueness of the right-derived extension applied to the natural evaluation isomorphism

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] to $\mathcal B$, $M=P$, the bounded-below $F$, the resolution $e$ of step 2, and $n=a$. The enough-injectives hypothesis was verified in step 2, and the chosen $I$ has all the stated properties. Its cocycle formula sends the class of $f_s$ to $Qe[a]^{-1}\circ Q(f_s:P[0]\to I[a])$. Together with step 3, this computes the normalized supported-Hom map:
$$\chi^a_{i,F}(x)=Qe[a]^{-1}\circ Q(f_s:P[0]\to I[a]).$$
There is no projectivity requirement on $P$ in the cited statement.

source.place: Tags 06XR (derived-Hom cocycle formula) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); the specified cocycle normalization

proof.text:
Compute the other transpose with the canonical derived adjunction of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. Let $\widetilde s:A[-a]\to G(I)$ be the complex map taking $1$ in degree $a$ to $s$. The morphism representing $x$ is $RG(Qe)^{-1}\beta_I Q\widetilde s$. By [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], the derived counit $\varepsilon'$ satisfies
$$\varepsilon'_{QI}\circ C_i(\beta_I)=Q(\varepsilon^0_I)$$
after the canonical exact-$C_i$ localization identifications, where $\varepsilon^0_I:C_i(GI)\to I$ is the termwise underived counit. This is exactly its stated counit equation, with the comparison for the exact left functor identified with the identity; the required derived adjunction and comparisons are the ones fixed in the definition. Naturality of $\varepsilon'$ with respect to $Qe$ therefore gives
$$x^\flat=Qe^{-1}\circ Q(\varepsilon^0_I)\circ Q(C_i(\widetilde s)).$$
The complex map $\varepsilon^0_I C_i(\widetilde s):P[-a]\to I$ has only one possibly nonzero component, in degree $a$. That component is the underived adjoint of $A\to G(I^a)$, $1\mapsto s$, hence is $f_s$ by step 1. It is a complex map because $G(d_I^a)s=0$ and step 1 is natural in $I^a$.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); normalized derived counit on representatives

proof.text:
Shift the formula of step 5 by $[a]$. With the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the map $P[-a]\to I$ having component $f_s$ in degree $a$ shifts to the map $P[0]\to I[a]$ having the identical component $f_s$ in degree zero. Shift changes differentials, not the components of a degree-zero complex map. Thus
$$x^\flat[a]=Qe[a]^{-1}\circ Q(f_s:P[0]\to I[a])=\chi^a_{i,F}(x)$$
by step 4. Explicitly, if $s$ is replaced by $s+G(d_I^{a-1})t$, step 1 replaces $f_s$ by $f_s+d_I^{a-1}f_t$. On the unshifted maps $P[-a]\to I$ this difference has homotopy component $f_t$ in degree $a$, while on $P[0]\to I[a]$ it has homotopy component $(-1)^a f_t$ in degree zero, since $d_{I[a]}=(-1)^a d_I$. Thus the equality uses exactly the stated cocycle convention for every integer $a$. All maps were obtained from the same natural evaluation bijection, establishing also the equivalent formulation.

source.place: Coherent shift convention and explicit boundary homotopy; final comparison

lean.note: The natural isomorphism is specified existentially together with its injective-cocycle evaluation normalization. The equality is quantified over all morphisms A[-a] → RΓ_Z(F); evaluation of degree-a cohomology at 1 is the inverse of the stipulated class-to-morphism identification. Thus it states χ(x)=x^flat[a] for every class, with no arbitrary choice of an unnormalized supported-Hom isomorphism.
